commits.subject: fix(picks): Warmup no longer terminally locks an undelivered pick
commits.body:
2026-08-13 incident: the 12:35 lineup check finished at 12:49, by which
point the double-down game (13:10 start) had entered MLB's Warmup state.
Warmup (statusCode PW) is abstract-Live but pre-first-pitch — the only
such state (all "Delayed Start:*" remain abstract-Preview) — so
classify_pick_lock_state marked the undelivered candidate
game_started_or_final, delivery was skipped, and the day passed silently
with both would-be legs hitting (Arraez 3-for-5, Meidroth 2-for-3).

- _classify_unposted_game_status: Warmup -> not locked
  (warmup_not_started). Matches statusCode "PW" first (now plumbed
  through get_game_statuses_detailed as "code"); exact detailed-string
  "warmup" kept as compatibility fallback for cached shapes.
- pick_candidate_status_is_available deliberately still EXCLUDES warmup:
  contest entry closes T-5 before scheduled first pitch, so the fresh
  pool stays conservative while an already-chosen candidate remains
  deliverable (Codex review: separate predicates, not one).
- classify_pick_lock_state: an undelivered pick with
  delivery_attempted=True now locks on that durable marker BEFORE any
  status lookup. Without this, the warmup carve-out (and the
  pre-existing Preview path) let select_pick reselect and overwrite the
  marker with delivery_attempted=False — erasing the crash-gap
  idempotency guard and re-sending (duplicate-delivery path).
- select_pick: when the fresh pool is empty but the existing pick itself
  classified deliverable, return it UNLOCKED so the fallback-deadline
  path can deliver it — returning it locked recreates the silent pass
  when the pick's own games are merely in warmup.
- The abstract-only fallback path (detailed lookup failed) still treats
  Warmup as locked: it cannot distinguish PW from in-progress, and
  fail-closed is deliberate there.

3 Codex review rounds (gpt-5.6-sol high); scheduler-side alert fixes in
the follow-up commit.

commits.subject: fix(scheduler): undelivered locked days must alert; commits must be durable
commits.body:
Companion to the Warmup classifier fix — the alerting half of the
2026-08-13 silent pass. Every safety net keyed off the wrong flag: E3
was gated on state.pick_locked, which a NON-delivered classification
lock sets without any delivery, so the alert never fired;
check-pick-entered correctly keys on scoreable commits and said
"nothing to check" all day.

- Step 5b now gates on committed_pick_written, and
  _maybe_alert_missed_pick additionally consults the on-disk
  decision.json (the authority — the in-memory flag can be stale after
  a crash between decision write and state save). Private mode still
  alerts on an UNCOMMITTED day by design (test-pinned D6 behavior; the
  operator enters manually, so silence is the incident class); a
  successful private lock is suppressed via its scoreable record.
- run_single_check pre-cascade: any scoreable decision on disk locks
  the day regardless of game status — a same-day restart must not
  reselect over a private/unconfirmed commit whose pick file carries no
  delivery flags (committed means immutable).
- _write_classification_decision: an undelivered pick classified locked
  on its delivery_attempted marker now finalizes as a scoreable
  locked_unconfirmed commit — the classifier locks on the durable
  marker before _deliver_and_lock_pick can run its unconfirmed-attempt
  branch after a restart, so finalization has to happen at the
  chokepoint (restores result polling + E3 suppression). Also never
  clobbers an existing scoreable decision with a source="unknown"
  recovery record; it resyncs the flag instead.
- _write_commit_decision: committed_pick_written is set only when
  write_decision actually returned a record — a flag with no record
  behind it suppressed E3 while leaving nothing for polling.

3 Codex review rounds; rejected finding recorded: blanket private-mode
E3 suppression (contradicts pinned D6 flip test; alert-on-ambiguity is
the safe direction after a silent pass — Codex withdrew on this).
